question: What can word subspace represent?

answer.free_form_answer: Word vectors, usually in the context of others within the same class
evidence: To tackle this problem, we introduce the novel concept of word subspace. It is mathematically defined as a low dimensional linear subspace in a word vector space with high dimensionality. Given that words from texts of the same class belong to the same context, it is possible to model word vectors of each class as word subspaces and efficiently compare them in terms of similarity by using canonical angles between the word subspaces. Through this representation, most of the variability of the class is retained. Consequently, a word subspace can effectively and compactly represent the context of the corresponding text. We achieve this framework through the mutual subspace method (MSM) BIBREF9 .

title: Text Classification based on Word Subspace with Term-Frequency
answer_short: the context or semantic content of texts by modeling word vectors from similar contexts in a low-dimensional linear subspace
answer_rationale: Text 2 explicitly defines a word subspace as a low-dimensional linear subspace in a word vector space that represents the context or semantic content of texts by modeling word vectors from similar contexts. It further states that this representation retains most of the variability of the class and allows efficient comparison of texts via canonical angles between subspaces.
